extracted.intended_audience: general literate readers; aspiring humorists and writers
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and principles for composing effective wit and humour in prose (especially short essays/letters), focusing on tone, diction, surprise, and imagery. Draws contrasts with common bad practices of both low 'cant' and overlearned pedantry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious countenance for delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jest is never uttered with a better Grace, than when it is accompanied with a serious Countenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver jokes with gravity rather than jocularity; a solemn face preserves surprise and enhances effect. Avoid smirking or telegraphing the joke before the line is delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid showing the thought before speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: When a pleasant Thought plays in the Features, before it discovers itself in Words, it raises too great an Expectation, and loses the Advantage of giving Surprize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let facial expression or preamble reveal the humourous idea; preserve the element of surprise by letting the thought emerge in the wording rather than in manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid levity of phrase and cant
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and Humour are no less poorly recommended by a Levity of Phrase, and that kind of Language which may be distinguished by the Name of Cant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of affected, slangy, or catchphrase-heavy diction (cant). Such pert phrases often show vivacity but substitute liveliness for genuine wit and pall the humour rather than heighten it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal ridicule in gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ridicule is never more strong, than when it is concealed in Gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mask satirical or ridiculing content within a serious tone; the contrast between solemn delivery and absurd content increases the force of ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour should arise from thought and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: True Humour lies in the Thought, and arises from the Representation of Images in odd Circumstances, and uncommon Lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize original comic ideas and striking images—the juxtaposition of incongruous situations—over merely witty phrasing. Develop the underlying conceit or image that generates the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural beauty of the thought over ridiculous phraseology
rubrics_metrics.description: A pleasant Thought strikes us by the Force of its natural Beauty; and the Mirth of it is generally rather palled, than heightened by that ridiculous Phraseology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clear, naturally appealing ideas; avoid dressing them up with forced or ridiculous verbal flourishes that can blunt their comedic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superficial theatrical affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: This Tribe of Men are like our Mountebanks; they make a Man a Wit, by putting him in a fantastick Habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't manufacture humour by adopting odd costumes, mannerisms, or theatrical poses; contrived external affectations do not substitute for genuine wit and often expose the weakness of the comic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the two extremes: pert phraseology and pedantic pomp
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two Extreams in the Stile of Humour, one ... the Use of that little pert Phraseology ... the other in the Affectation of strained and pompous Expressions, fetched from the learned Languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither cheap, pert slang nor overblown classical/learned diction serves true humour. Both extremes—town-cant vivacity and college-pedantry—undermine comic effect; aim for a balanced, natural style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't obscure humour with overlearned diction (pedantick humour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedantick Humour uses strained, pompous Expressions and riddling allusions that force the reader to puzzle twice or thrice before understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive classical references, obscure metaphors, or deliberately riddle-like wording that makes the joke hard to parse. Clarity aids comedic timing and recognition; humour that requires decoding often fails to amuse.
